oneLine: NSE IPO features an all-OFS structure providing liquidity to existing shareholders.
seller: existing shareholders including State Bank of India, Bank of Baroda, and Canada Pension Plan Investment Board

sources.title: NSE IPO: Can the large supply of shares and all-OFS structure limit listing gains?

synopsis: The National Stock Exchange has launched a Rs 22,569 crore initial public offering structured entirely as an offer for sale by existing shareholders, including State Bank of India, Bank of Baroda, and Canada Pension Plan Investment Board. Existing shareholders are selling up to 12.64 crore shares at an upper price band of Rs 1,785 apiece. The NSE will not receive any proceeds from the issue. The offer opened on September 17 and is scheduled to close on September 21, with shares expected to list on the BSE on September 24. Analysts are divided on whether the all-OFS structure and large supply of shares will limit immediate listing-day gains, amid a cooling grey market premium.
